system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Competition: Tech, Money and Regional Wars Reshape Order
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system in flux where a ferocious tech/AI and industrial arms race intersects with volatile financial markets, strategic resource competition and regionally concentrated kinetic conflicts. Monetary interventions, trade and industrial policy, climate-driven resource shocks and cyber/AI risks are propagating feedbacks across markets, supply chains and security architectures, raising the probability of accidental escalations and disorderly economic adjustments. Major powers (US, China, Russia, EU, regional blocs) and large corporates act as amplifiers, while weaker states, migration flows and climate extremes create vulnerable seams. Expect cascading interactions rather than single-point shocks: a ruin in one domain (energy, currency, AI, or a regional strike) will transmit quickly through finance, trade and domestic politics.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and alliances; major corporations and tech platforms; global financial markets and central banks; energy, commodities and semiconductor supply chains; regional kinetic conflicts (Middle East, Ukraine, East Asia); global trade and migration flows; cyber and AI security incidents; climate and extreme-weather impacts on infrastructure and food supplies; multilateral institutions and informal diplomatic channels.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-ecological-economic system (global civilization embedded in the Earth system: climate, biosphere, resource base).

variables.name: Global AI competition and governance
variables.description: The United States, China, the EU and major tech firms are contesting dominance in advanced AI — from massive models and compute investments to emergent 'rogue AI' risks — prompting shifts in corporate strategy and tighter state oversight.

variables.name: Strait of Hormuz security standoff
variables.description: Iran, Gulf states, the US and regional partners are clashing over freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran's threats and strikes and parallel Oman-led talks altering maritime rules and risking oil-flow disruptions.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and escalation risks
variables.description: Russia, Ukraine and NATO actors remain locked in high-intensity conflict, with renewed strikes, persistent supply and munitions pressures and growing risks of spillover that could test allied resolve.

variables.name: US–China economic and industrial rivalry
variables.description: Washington and Beijing are deepening strategic competition across trade, tariffs, export controls and incentives for critical materials and industries (energy inputs, batteries, semiconductors), accelerating supply‑chain reconfiguration and partial decoupling.

variables.name: Currency and market intervention volatility
variables.description: Major central banks and governments — notably the US, Japan and the ECB — are increasingly intervening or signaling interventions in currencies and bond markets, marking a shift toward active 'currency activism' that is amplifying yield, gold and cross‑border financial volatility.
